chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man sneezes, let one say, 'All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds, there is no associate for Him.' And when the man says the response, let him say, 'May Allah have mercy on you.' And when he responds, let him say, 'May Allah forgive you and us.' For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was asked about a verse or something wherein was a mention of Allah, so he said: 'Whenever Allah is mentioned therein, it is excellent.'

key_terms.يَرْحَمُكَ اللَّهُ: May Allah have mercy on you

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications for sneezing and responding in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the ritual etiquette (adab) of sneezing, prescribing the response 'Yarhamuk Allah' and the reply 'Yaghfiru Allahu laka wa lana,' reflecting the communal bond of seeking forgiveness. It grounds this practice in the Prophet’s teaching that any mention of Allah is inherently virtuous, a principle Shia scholars link to the sanctity of divine names in daily life. The inclusion of 'wa lana' in the response highlights the intercessory nature of supplication within the Shia tradition.
